problem_statement: When the updated OSTest hrtimer test is run in a NuttX configuration that enables hrtimer support, the hrtimer_test case does not complete and ostest times out. The test change in testing/ostest/hrtimer.c updates the checks for hrtimer_cancel and hrtimer_cancel_sync to accept a non-negative return value, but the observed behavior is that the hrtimer test hangs instead of reaching completion and returning status 0. The issue is reproducible with hrtimer enabled and is not confined to tickless operation; it also affects tick-based operation, and tickless operation with hrtimer is not properly supported. The required behavior is that hrtimer functionality works regardless of the scheduler tick mode: hrtimer_cancel and hrtimer_cancel_sync must complete with results accepted by the updated test, the hrtimer_test case must pass, and ostest should terminate normally in both tick-based and tickless configurations.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: With hrtimer enabled on sim:nsh, the ostest hrtimer test asserts hrtimer_cancel() and hrtimer_cancel_sync() return exactly OK, which fails because these functions return the timer reference count (>= 0) and the previous hrtimer update had restricted hardware timer reprogramming to tickless mode only, breaking hrtimer in tick-based mode. The test must accept any non-negative return (ret >= 0) and require correct hrtimer reprogramming behavior so the suite passes on a tick-based scheduler.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "the previous hrtimer update had restricted hardware timer reprogramming to tickless mode only, breaking hrtimer in tick-based mode"; "The test must accept any non-negative return (ret >= 0) and require correct hrtimer reprogramming behavior so the suite passes on a tick-based scheduler.". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally
